sourceTranslationChanges.before: How many dedications are there? There are seven dedications, and these are they: the dedication of heaven and earth, as it says, “Heaven and earth were completed” (Genesis 2:1). What dedication was there? “God placed them in the firmament of heaven to give light” (Genesis 1:17 [the source’s parenthetical reads verse 18]). The dedication of the wall, as it says, “At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem” (Nechemiah 12:27). The dedication by those who returned from exile, as it says, “They offered for the dedication of this House of our God,” and so forth (Ezra 6:17). The dedication of the priests—this is the one for which we light lamps. The dedication of the World to Come, as it says, “I shall search Jerusalem with lamps” (Zephaniah 1:12). The dedication of the princes: “This was the dedication of the altar” (Numbers 7:84). And the dedication of the Temple, which was read in the passage: “A psalm, a song for the dedication of the House, of David.”
sourceTranslationChanges.after: How many dedications are there? There are seven dedications, and these are they: the dedication of heaven and earth, as it says, “Heaven and earth were completed” (Genesis 2:1). What dedication was there? “God placed them in the firmament of heaven to give light” (Genesis 1:17). The dedication of the wall, as it says, “At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem” (Nechemiah 12:27). The dedication by those who returned from exile, as it says, “They offered for the dedication of this House of our God,” and so forth (Ezra 6:17). The dedication of the priests—this is the one for which we light lamps. The dedication of the World to Come, as it says, “I shall search Jerusalem with lamps” (Zephaniah 1:12). The dedication of the princes: “This was the dedication of the altar” (Numbers 7:84). And the dedication of the Temple, which was read in the passage: “A psalm, a song for the dedication of the House, of David.”

sourceTranslationChanges.before: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: the Torah was given only to Moshe and his descendants, as it says, “Write for yourself,” and “Carve for yourself”: just as the offcuts are yours, so the writing is yours. Moshe acted generously with it and gave it to Israel; concerning him Scripture says, “The generous eye shall be blessed,” and so forth. Rav Chisda objected: “Hashem commanded me at that time to teach you.” [The response:] “He commanded me, and I [passed it on] to you.” “See, I have taught you statutes and judgments as Hashem my God commanded me.” [Again:] “He commanded me, and I [passed it on] to you.” “And now write this song for yourselves.” [The response:] “The song alone.” But [it says], “So that this song shall be a witness for Me among the children of Israel”! Rather, [what had been given to Moshe alone was] the art of incisive Torah reasoning.
sourceTranslationChanges.after: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: the Torah was given only to Moshe and his descendants, as it says, “Write for yourself,” and “Carve for yourself”: just as the offcuts are yours, so the writing is yours. Moshe acted generously with it and gave it to Israel; concerning him Scripture says, “The generous eye shall be blessed,” and so forth. Rav Chisda objected: “Hashem commanded me at that time to teach you.” The response was: “He commanded me, and I passed it on to you.” “See, I have taught you statutes and judgments as Hashem my God commanded me.” Again, the response was: “He commanded me, and I passed it on to you.” “And now write this song for yourselves.” The response was: “The song alone.” But it says, “So that this song shall be a witness for Me among the children of Israel”! Rather, what had been given to Moshe alone was the art of incisive Torah reasoning.

sourceTranslationChanges.before: He said to him: if a person makes himself like this wilderness, which everyone treads upon, Torah is given to him as a gift. Once it is given to him as a gift, God takes him as His portion, as it says, “From Mattanah, Nachaliel.” Once God takes him as His portion, he rises to greatness, as it says, “From Nachaliel, Bamot [heights].” If his heart becomes arrogant, the Holy One, blessed be He, lowers him, as it says, “From the heights, the valley.” If he turns back, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him, as it says, “Every valley shall be lifted.”

sourceTranslationChanges.before: Rabbi Oshaya said: what is the meaning of “I took for Myself two staffs; one I called Pleasantness, and one I called Wounders”? “Pleasantness” refers to the Torah scholars of the Land of Israel, who are pleasant with one another in halakhic discussion. “Wounders” refers to the Torah scholars of Babylonia, who wound one another in halakhic discussion. “He said to me: These are the [two] sons of oil who stand,” and so forth; “and two olive trees beside it.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: “Oil” refers to the Torah scholars of the Land of Israel, who are gentle with one another in halakhic discussion, like olive oil. “And two olive trees beside it” refers to the Torah scholars of Babylonia, who are bitter toward one another in halakhic discussion, like an olive.

sourceTranslationChanges.before: “Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven.” Trachinus—may his bones be ground to dust—had a wife who gave birth on the night of the Ninth of Av, while all Israel was mourning. The infant fell silent [died] at Chanukah. Israel said, “Shall we kindle the lamps or not?” They said, “We shall kindle them; whatever may come upon us, let it come.” They kindled them. People went and spoke maliciously to the wife of Trachinus: “These Jews mourned when you gave birth, but when the child died, they kindled lamps.”
